<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915147_theRebbe_734" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915147_theRebbe_734__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The sitra achra has an eleventh aspect separate from its ten, and correspondingly in holiness there is a level above the ten Sefiros that is separate from them, which is the source for refining the eleven impurities of Esav.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the sitra achra is parallel to this in holiness.</t>
    <t s="1">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that just as in impurity there is a level that is an eleventh that is separate from the ten,</t>
    <t s="3">so too in holiness there is correspondingly,</t>
    <t s="4">that there is a level that is above the ten Sefiros and separate from them.</t>
    <t s="5">[However, in holiness,</t>
    <t s="6">this level is not the life-force of the ten Sefiros</t>
    <t s="7">[for the life-force of the ten Sefiros is invested within them and unified with them as above.</t>
    <t s="8">And the aspect of the encompassing light that is above the ten Sefiros is a matter unto itself19]</t>
    <t s="9">Therefore it is not counted with them,</t>
    <t s="10">“You are One and not in number”20,</t>
    <t s="11">but not so in the sitra achra,</t>
    <t s="12">where the aspect of the encompassing light is their life-force,</t>
    <t s="13">it is necessary to include also the encompassing light in their count</t>
    <t s="14">(for without the encompassing light they have no life-force21),</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore they are eleven in number].</t>
    <t s="16">And based on this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="17">that the refinement of the eleven crowns of impurity is through the drawing down of the encompassing light that is above the ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="18">which is not counted with them</t>
    <t s="19">(the aspect of Atik22),</t>
    <t s="20">corresponding to the eleventh level in the sitra achra that is separate from them as above.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is “And may God give you from the dew of the heavens,”</t>
    <t s="22">for the first matter in Yitzchak’s blessing is dew,</t>
    <t s="23">the dew of Atika23,</t>
    <t s="24">because in order to refine the sparks that are in Esav, it is through the drawing down of the aspect of Atik,</t>
    <t s="25">as above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The drawing down of Atik below to refine the sparks of the sitra achra is specifically through the drawing down of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above even Atik.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, in order for there to be a drawing down of Atik below, to the extent that through this there will be a refinement of the sparks in the sitra achra,</t>
    <t s="2">it is specifically through the drawing down of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above even Atik.</t>
    <t s="3">For Atik in and of itself,</t>
    <t s="4">since its matter is that it is removed and separate from the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="5">(Atik from the term “removed”24),</t>
    <t s="6">it is impossible for it to be drawn down below,</t>
    <t s="7">and in order for it to be drawn down below, it is specifically through the Essence of Ein Sof, which is not defined by any definition.</t>
    <t s="8">And based on this, the superiority and novelty of Yitzchak’s blessing “And may God give you etc.” over “And God blessed Yitzchak” will be understood,</t>
    <t s="9">for the blessing “And may God give you” is that there should be a drawing down below to refine the sparks that are in Esav,</t>
    <t s="10">and this drawing down is from the Essence of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="11">as above.</t>
    <t s="12">And this is “And may God give you”</t>
    <t s="13">(Elokim with the definite article),</t>
    <t s="14">the aspect of the essential concealment of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="15">from which is the power of refinements25.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The blessing of Yitzchak for “dew of the heavens” refers to the toil in Torah that reaches beyond the Torah as it is in itself, to the essential concealment.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is26 what is stated in the Midrash27</t>
    <t s="1">“From the dew of the heavens — this is Scripture, and from the fat of the earth — this is Mishnah, grain — this is Talmud, etc.,”</t>
    <t s="2">for at first glance it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="3">for even without Yitzchak’s blessing, the Torah would have been given to Israel,</t>
    <t s="4">since the purpose of creation was for Israel to receive the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the act of creation, etc., “If Israel accepts the Torah, etc.”28,</t>
    <t s="5">and what is it that he blessed him with Torah?</t>
    <t s="6">And the explanation of this is known,</t>
    <t s="7">that Yitzchak’s blessing was concerning the matter of toil in Torah, through which one reaches a level above the aspect of Torah as it is in itself.</t>
    <t s="8">For the Torah in itself is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="9">and higher still — the concealed wisdom,</t>
    <t s="10">and through toil in Torah,</t>
    <t s="11">toil in the manner of returning light,</t>
    <t s="12">one reaches the essential concealment</t>
    <t s="13">(of Torah),</t>
    <t s="14">“No eye has seen, O God, besides You”29.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
